scope: Read-only source and design feasibility review; no repository edits, builds, Cargo, QEMU, USB operations, or product changes by reviewer.

decision.this_round: Freeze existing product. Add only an independent two-guest SIGKILL negative observation and the first no-IMPORT restart observation. Preserve the initial baseline and actual FAIL independently of evidence-collection completion. No recovery guard, persistent lease, guardian, or automatic restore is implemented by the draft.
decision.next_product_slice_candidate: A root-helper-owned, bounded persistent delegation ledger preventing a new grant from silently replacing an unresolved original baseline. It must include a normal verified retirement/reconciliation path in the same product slice; a permanent deny with no usable release path is not a complete fix.
decision.automatic_restore: Defer until ownership, process/capability lifetime, trustworthy original intent, configuration/alternate ambiguity, and helper restart semantics have been designed and tested.
decision.phase_boundary: Requirements 4.5 and exceptional-exit testing justify this work now; it is not acceptance of complete Phase 2, Phase 3 authentication/encryption/state management, Phase 5 service packaging, Windows, storage recovery, or physical G1/G2.

current_source_facts.fact: Helper App serializes its operations but OpenPhysical does not insert a physical ownership/delegation record. serve_connection holds PhysicalGrant only until one JSON/ACK/SCM_RIGHTS exchange completes, then drops its reference. Helper restart reconstructs only empty in-memory Native ManagedState.

PhysicalGrant and GrantDescription contain an open FD, Device and PhysicalDeviceReceipt. Device has selected interface alternates/drivers but no active configuration field; a trustworthy helper recovery baseline needs an additional coherent configuration observation.

Ordinary process initialize constructs originals from the current helper Device, reads current configuration, matches current drivers, and starts available/cleanup_verified=true. This is a fresh registry baseline, not proof that an earlier process restored its originals. Actual acceptance on the first restart is still to be measured.

IMPORT acquires interfaces using no_reattach. The in-process worker alone remembers acquired original interfaces and configuration_changed. Normal restore waits real terminals, performs checked releases, rejects uncertain external state, and independently checks original config/alt/drivers.

SIGTERM changes retain the original cleanup owner. SIGKILL cannot execute that application cleanup; process exit, client VHCI auto-NULL, and socket EOF do not by themselves establish server driver/config/alt restoration.

Same-generation scanner checks and per-interface reobservation already reject foreign usbfs/usbip-host, unsafe configuration, mismatching original driver, and replug generations during normal cleanup. Recovery must preserve these checks rather than introduce a force-unbind escape hatch.

mechanisms.mechanism: Retain the original SCM_RIGHTS FD or dup
mechanisms.assessment: Not a separate recovery capability. It shares the USBFS open file description. Keeping it alive prevents final close of that usb_dev_state and can retain the old claim/async queues after service death. Do not assume both retained duplicate and automatic final-close cleanup. Reaping the old nusb user-pointer completions in another process would require a separate carefully audited design; do not transplant pointer values.

mechanisms.mechanism: Independently open the same current USB device
mechanisms.assessment: Gets a different usb_dev_state; it can preserve a generation-scoped potential recovery handle, but cannot RELEASEINTERFACE for another open. An existing foreign driver/usbfs claim is a refusal condition. CONNECT only asks the kernel to probe; it is not a command naming the original driver and must be checked afterwards.

mechanisms.mechanism: Ordinary parent supervising its fixed child
mechanisms.assessment: Smallest process-death prototype and preserves non-root data path. A real child wait avoids recycled-PID guesses. Still requires independent recovery capability, original-state transfer, backpressure-safe control and explicit parent-death handling. It covers child failure only; parent death/host restart lose volatile intent. A journal-free supervisor must be marketed only for that narrower fault model.

mechanisms.mechanism: Root helper retaining an independent recovery FD and lease
mechanisms.assessment: Matches the existing FD authorization boundary and avoids launching network USB/IP parsers as root. It adds sensitive lifecycle work, resource bounds and locking to helper. Its own death closes the independent handle; a new helper needs a persistent unresolved record and must not reopen a reused Bus ID automatically. PIDFD/socket EOF is a notification, not revocation or proof of last reference.

mechanisms.mechanism: Persistent delegation journal and restart reconciliation
mechanisms.assessment: Best initial durable safety boundary: preserve trusted originals and deny silent rebaselining. The journal is intent/evidence, not kernel truth or authority to force restore. A file/rename alone is not durable publication; failure must prevent grant, and updates require file plus containing-directory synchronization under a documented supported filesystem boundary.

threat_model.trusted_current_premise: Root/host kernel and protected helper policy are trusted. The ordinary USBFS server is trusted to exercise its delegated whole-device write FD; no existing per-URB sandbox or revocation exists. New ledger design must not silently claim it can contain a malicious process retaining/passing that FD.
adversarial_or_concurrent_inputs: Unauthorised UID or fabricated lease/generation/finish request
Malformed, oversized, unknown-version, symlinked or insecure state file
Failure/crash between durable publication, grant send, client receive, cleanup verification and retirement
Concurrent approved server requesting the same device before either IMPORT
External usbip-host/usbfs/other driver acquisition, configuration change, or replug using same fingerprint/Bus ID/address
Helper or supervisor death; inherited/SCM-passed duplicate capability outliving the original service
outside_claimed_protection: Forced recovery of active storage, mounted filesystems, or data consistency
Guaranteed termination of an uninterruptible in-kernel operation
Revocation of already delegated whole-device FDs
Transparent restoration of all multi-configuration/nondefault alternate histories without operation provenance

normal_path_must_be_preserved: Do not ban all driver=None baselines. Legitimately unbound approved devices remain representable. Reject unresolved history by trusted record and receipt, not by treating None as evidence of crash.

Do not require a single configuration or alt0 globally. Existing ECM multiple configuration/alternate behavior remains available to the live authorized service. A deny-only unresolved ledger need not journal every USB control request because it performs no automatic restoration.

One grant/record covers the service registration lifetime and its multiple IMPORT/cleanup cycles. An IMPORT lease is not the same lifecycle as the helper delegation; their names/state must distinguish them.

Normal stop and no-IMPORT stop must have a real bounded retirement path, followed by an ordinary second start and actual I/O. Setup failure after one of up to 16 grants, cancelled prepare and bind/output failures also require explicit cleanup/record disposition.

Do not clear a record merely because a client asserts cleanup_verified, outputs stopped, closes its control socket, or exits. Helper must independently check the stored baseline and decide the remaining-capability trust/lifetime boundary. This decision is still open, not solved by this report.

An old generation record must never authorize recovery on replug. Preserve the old record as gone/stale and require a newly verified explicit grant; do not overwrite the old baseline or apply a blanket device-ID deny forever without a reconciliation path.

must_resolve_before_product_implementati.issue: Normal retirement authority and capability lifetime
must_resolve_before_product_implementati.required_decision: Specify which authenticated process may finish which record, when all relevant backend FD owners have been dropped, how helper independently verifies config/alternates/driver/generation/full safety, and what residual FD-duplication assumption remains. A client boolean or PID death is insufficient. Test both ordinary second start and refusal while a retained-capability test process still owns an interface.

Helper, not request JSON, captures original config plus exact full interface/alt/driver set and generation under bounded coherent pre/post observation. Current Device lacks active config. Do not persist serial strings/raw USB data unnecessarily; store only bounded restoration metadata under root-only protection.

Reserve per generation and persist unresolved state before the FD may escape, including queued ancillary rights. Unknown send/ACK outcomes remain unresolved. Do not delete on timeout/EOF merely because receive was not acknowledged. Prevent a concurrent second grant before first service claims USB.

Fixed protected path; strict schema/version/size limits; singleton helper or cross-instance store exclusion; atomic durable publish/retire; read-only status on corruption. Missing first-install store vs lost established store needs a documented initialization/migration distinction; silent empty-default after failure reopens the gap.

must_resolve_before_product_implementati.issue: Identity across daemon and host restart
must_resolve_before_product_implementati.required_decision: Persist boot identity or an equivalent boot boundary. Current dev/inode/USB-address receipt is within one kernel instance, not cross-boot identity. Never auto-apply old restoration on changed boot/generation; fresh explicit authorization must preserve historical evidence.

must_resolve_before_product_implementati.issue: Usable reconciliation after crash before Finish
must_resolve_before_product_implementati.required_decision: Keep an unresolved record on doubt, but provide bounded observation/admin reconciliation and safe retirement criteria. Permanent denial after a normally restored process crashed just before Finish is conservative degradation, not full recovery. Any reset/forget action must be explicit, root-authorized, and not disguise device writes.

For auto-write recovery, initial baseline alone cannot show whether a changed config belongs to this service or an external actor. Need proven owned mutation range with before/intent/observed outcome ordering, or quarantine uncertain changes. Preserve None+nonzero-alt limitation; generic CONNECT cannot guarantee exact original driver.

draft_review.decision: No must-fix for launching the bounded negative observation described in the draft. Not ready as an implementation contract for a durable guard or automatic recovery.
draft_review.required_wording: Current round is source review plus independent negative runtime evidence only. Future unresolved-lease guard must include normal verified retirement and usable reconciliation. Never claim the guard/recovery already exists.
negative_contract_notes: SIGKILL wait137 is a process-termination fact, not recovery PASS/FAIL by itself. Finish both guest collection paths before verdict.
Require fixed full observation window even when original driver not restored; absence of stopped means final backend counts unknown, not zero and not permanent leak.
Restart is a distinct first observation only, no IMPORT and no destructive pre-cleanup. Initial baseline stays immutable; a restarted ready cleanup_verified means only its own registry semantics.
If restart fails, save actual error/exit/FD/sysfs and do not retry until evidence is complete. If ready, capture before any control input and then cooperate-stop, collecting post-stop external state.
Guard input/source/ELF and helper PID/identity against accidental helper restart or stale process substitution.

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Existing product SIGKILL after real HID+FTDI I/O and pending URBs
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Exact owned service identity, before original/generation/claims/budget, single KILL and actual wait, fixed observation window, independent server sysfs and client auto-disconnect before detach, missing stopped preserved
acceptance_matrix.expected_status: Actual product recovery verdict, never converted by test collection success

acceptance_matrix.scenario: First restart on same IDs without IMPORT
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Same helper, no pre-repair; actual ready/original/current/cleanup_verified or exact refusal; FD and independent sysfs; cooperative stop and post-stop; initial original snapshot retained
acceptance_matrix.expected_status: Observation only; no blanket expected acceptance and no recovery claim

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Normal service and no-IMPORT start/stop, each followed by second start and real I/O
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Durable initial record, helper-verified retirement, no leaked deny; multi-device partial setup paths also bounded
acceptance_matrix.expected_status: PASS required before calling ledger a usable fix

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Existing ECM multiple configuration and alt behavior
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Current protocol/UDP/config/alt/driver restoration regressions still pass; no new singleconfig/None rejection

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Crash at grant reserve/publish/send/receive and restored-before-retire
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Each actual failpoint; no escaped unrecorded FD; unresolved preserved; explicit normal reconciliation recovery path
acceptance_matrix.expected_status: No blind new baseline or silent erase

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Concurrent grants and duplicated/inherited service capability
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Only one live delegation per current generation; old holder continues to own claim in retained-FD case and new grant/retire is refused

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Helper KILL/restart with live or unresolved delegation
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Old ability may remain; durable rows survive and new helper observes but does not steal; stale socket handled explicitly
acceptance_matrix.expected_status: Refuse ambiguous reuse; preserve actual live data behavior

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Truncated/version-invalid/insecure journal, missing established store, disk/full/fsync/rename errors
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: No device FD grant on failed publication or corrupt state; Native/read-only diagnostics disposition documented; originals not overwritten

acceptance_matrix.scenario: External usbfs, usbip-host, different driver/config takeover
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Refusal with zero forced unbind/config writes; unrelated device I/O continues

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Replug same fingerprint/Bus ID and helper vs full host restart
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Old receipt rejected; old record retained; changed boot not mistaken for matching inode; only explicit new verified grant can authorize current generation

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Forged finish/lease fields from unauthorized or wrong owner and stale replay
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: No record deletion/grant/device operation; exact current policy and actor check; repeated successful finish idempotent

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Child death with independent FD vs same-OFD retained duplicate
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Separate open identities and kernel state; same-OFD case does not assume final-close cleanup; real terminal and drivers observed

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Crash during configuration/alternate change and successful/failed raw IOCTL
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Trusted intent and actual outcome or quarantine; no blind rollback from current value alone; external changes refused

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Composite sibling probe, original=None, nonzero alternate
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Per-interface reobserve and exact original outcome; currently unsupported None+nonzero case remains explicit

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Supervisor death, helper death during recovery, repeated recovery and bounded kernel stall
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Durable unresolved state and idempotent observations; no future-drop-as-cancellation or claim of terminating kernel wait

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Physical G1/G2, real serial/HID/other devices, storage, successful clear/partial, kernel-internal active window
acceptance_matrix.required_evidence: Separate explicit environment/device authorization and evidence
acceptance_matrix.expected_status: QEMU does not close these gates

sources.checked: Pinned v6.8 source plus existing local copy, functions usbdev_open/usbdev_release/releaseintf/proc_setconfig/proc_ioctl; Ubuntu guest behavior not inferred as already run.
SCM_RIGHTS transfers a reference to an open file description, equivalent to duplication.
PIDFD process observation and child/PID-reuse conditions; not FD capability lifetime or authorization.
Directory entry durability requires directory fsync in addition to file sync.

review_limits: Source-level feasibility and threat-model review only; no new runtime outcomes.
Root is intentionally drafting docs concurrently; observed docs-dirty is not a product source freeze failure.
Exact journal/API/retirement protocol remains proposed and must be refined after actual negative observation.
No full security platform, systemd packaging, TLS/authentication, storage recovery, or generalized supervisor introduced.
